about: Disc images worth burning, picked for people who remember when a CD-R was cutting-edge technology. Every image here may be freely redistributed. The depot only links to each project's own downloads; a monthly job fetches every image, records its size and SHA-256, and Krouton refuses a download that doesn't match.

channels.title: The shelf, 1998 to 2010
channels.about: Systems from the years when a burner was the fastest way to share software and every magazine came with a disc.

channels.title: Strange and wonderful
channels.about: Tiny systems, whole operating systems written in assembly, and a Linux that saves itself back onto the disc it booted from.

channels.title: Fix-it discs
channels.about: Boot a broken computer, test its memory, rescue its files, or wipe it before it leaves the house.

channels.title: Console homebrew
channels.about: Open-source tools for the GameCube, Wii, Dreamcast and PlayStation: boot discs that burn on a CD-R or DVD-R, and SD-card tools for making 1:1 backups of discs you own. No games: bring your own. A Wii only reads burned DVDs with a modchip, and only on the early drive models; DVD+R discs would also need their book type set to DVD-ROM, which Krouton doesn't do, so use DVD-R.

items.title: Ubuntu 4.10 "Warty Warthog" live CD
items.summary: The first Ubuntu, released in October 2004, back when Canonical posted free pressed CDs to anyone who asked. The live CD was a separate disc from the installer, and booted to GNOME 2.8 with the brown "Human" theme.

items.title: Ubuntu 6.06 "Dapper Drake" desktop CD
items.summary: The first long-term-support Ubuntu and the first where one CD both ran live and installed. For many people, this was the disc that arrived in the post.

items.title: Damn Small Linux 4.4.10
items.summary: A whole graphical desktop in about 50 MB, small enough for a business-card CD. It runs on a 486 with 16 MB of RAM, which made it the standard way to bring an old laptop back to life.

burn.note: Fits on a 50 MB business-card CD or an 8 cm mini CD as well as a full-size disc.

items.title: Knoppix 9.1 CD edition
items.summary: Klaus Knopper's Knoppix made the live CD famous around 2000: boot a full Linux desktop without touching the hard disk, with remarkably good hardware detection. It is still maintained, and the CD edition still fits on a 700 MB disc.

items.title: FreeDOS 1.4 live CD
items.summary: An open-source DOS that runs the games and utilities of the early 1990s on real hardware. The live CD boots straight to a DOS prompt, with the option to install, and comes with editors, compilers and network tools.

items.title: Haiku R1/beta5
items.summary: The open-source continuation of BeOS, the fast, quirky operating system Be Inc. offered as a free "Personal Edition" download in 2000. Haiku keeps the yellow window tabs, the Deskbar and the instant boot.

items.title: ReactOS live CD
items.summary: An open-source operating system that aims to run Windows programs and drivers, and looks like Windows 2000 while doing it. Still alpha software, so try it in a virtual machine or a spare PC.

items.title: Puppy Linux 4.3.1: the live CD that saves itself back to the disc
items.summary: Puppy loads entirely into RAM, which frees the drive it booted from. At shutdown it can write your session back onto that same disc as a new session, holding only the files that changed. The next boot loads the latest one, until the disc is full.

burn.note: Burn it with the disc left open for more sessions, or Puppy can't write back to it. DVD-R and DVD+R work best: each CD session wastes about 14 MB. On a rewritable disc, use a full erase to clear it, because a quick erase doesn't remove the old sessions properly.

items.title: KolibriOS
items.summary: A complete graphical operating system written in assembly language, with a desktop, web browser, games and a text editor, small enough to fit on a 1.44 MB floppy. The CD boots in a few seconds.

items.title: Tiny Core Linux
items.summary: A graphical Linux desktop in about 25 MB, by one of the original Damn Small Linux developers. Everything runs from RAM, and applications load as extensions only when you ask for them.

burn.note: Small enough for a business-card or 8 cm mini CD.

items.title: SliTaz GNU/Linux
items.summary: A complete desktop with a web browser in about 50 MB, built from scratch rather than from another distribution, and fast on machines from the early 2000s.

items.title: SystemRescue
items.summary: The successor to SystemRescueCD, a fixture of every technician's CD wallet since 2003. It boots to a toolkit for repairing partitions, file systems and boot loaders, with GParted, TestDisk, ddrescue and a web browser.

items.title: GParted Live
items.summary: Boots straight into the GParted partition editor: resize, move, copy and check partitions on a disk that isn't in use.

items.title: Rescuezilla
items.summary: Point-and-click disk backup, restore and cloning, compatible with Clonezilla images, plus a file browser for getting files off a computer that won't boot.

items.title: Memtest86+
items.summary: The memory tester that has been diagnosing random crashes since 2004. Version 7 boots on UEFI computers and current DDR5 hardware.

items.title: Darik's Boot and Nuke 2.3.0
items.summary: The classic way to wipe a hard disk before giving a computer away. It is unmaintained and can't securely erase SSDs; use ShredOS for modern drives.

items.title: ShredOS
items.summary: A tiny Linux that boots straight into nwipe, the maintained successor to DBAN's wiping engine, and can wipe several disks at once.

items.title: Super GRUB2 Disk
items.summary: Finds and boots operating systems on a computer whose boot loader is broken, so you can get in and repair it.

items.title: Swiss for GameCube: boot disc
items.summary: The all-in-one GameCube homebrew utility: it browses SD adapters, memory cards and the network, launches homebrew, and plays your own game backups with video-mode and region fixes. The boot disc image is for a GameCube with a modchip, which is what lets the console read a burned disc.

burn.note: GameCube discs are 8 cm. Burn to an 8 cm mini DVD-R; a full-size disc doesn't fit the tray.

items.title: Unirom boot disc for PlayStation
items.summary: Custom firmware for PlayStation cheat cartridges such as the Action Replay and GameShark. The boot disc installs it onto the cartridge or a memory card without opening the console, after which the PlayStation can boot homebrew and your own backups.
items.license: Free to use and share (see the project's licence)

burn.note: Burn the .cue/.bin as it is, in disc-at-once mode, at a slow speed. Without a modchip, start it with FreePSXBoot from a memory card instead.

items.title: DreamShell for Dreamcast
items.summary: A small operating system for the Dreamcast with a file manager, media player and a loader for games on an SD adapter or hard disk mod. Dreamcasts made before late 2000 boot burned CD-Rs without a modchip. Its boot disc is a two-session .cdi image, which Krouton can't burn yet, so get it from the project.

items.title: CleanRip for Wii
items.summary: Makes exact 1:1 copies of your own Wii and GameCube discs onto an SD card or USB drive, checked against the Redump database. Copy it to the apps folder of an SD card and run it from the Homebrew Channel.

items.title: USB Loader GX
items.summary: Plays your own Wii and GameCube backups from a USB drive, with cover art, per-game settings and parental controls.

items.title: Open PS2 Loader
items.summary: Plays your own PlayStation 2 backups from USB, the network or an internal hard disk, which spares the ageing DVD drive.

items.title: The Homebrew Channel (HackMii Installer)
items.summary: Where Wii homebrew starts: it installs the Homebrew Channel and BootMii, from which CleanRip and USB Loader GX run. The installer is free but its authors only offer it from their own site.
items.license: Free to use; redistribution not permitted

items.title: Wiimms ISO Tools (wit)
items.summary: Command-line tools for checking, converting and extracting Wii and GameCube images: ISO, WBFS, CISO and more. Useful for checking a dump before burning or copying it.
